body.statement: Fix \(\mathcal A\).  Let \(S=\{s_i=(i,\tau_i):i\in V\}\) contain exactly one temporal role for each coordinate, with \(s_X=(X,-\gamma)\) and \(s_Y=(Y,0)\).  Suppose two finite temporal-role semi-Markovian SCMs on \(S\) use the alphabets \(\mathcal A_i\), have legal lags bounded by \(L\), have a common strictly positive rational joint role law, have different probabilities of \(s_Y=y\) under \(\operatorname{do}(s_X=x)\), have acyclic unions of lag-zero coordinate relations, and have translation closures with exact common summary \(H\).  Then the independent-shift construction yields \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) such that \(P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\) as measures on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) and \(\theta_{M_0}(y;x)\ne\theta_{M_1}(y;x)\).
body.justification: This lemma turns a bounded graphical collision into the whole-process stationary countermodels required for semantic nonidentification.
body.gap: Shpitser--Pearl construct finite fixed-ADMG hedge models, while Jahn--Karnik--Schulman localize fixed-graph hedges; neither result preserves strict stationarity, time homogeneity, exact summaries, and equality of the entire process law under a refinement switch.
body.consumer: Every rejecting state of \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)\) obtains an auditable finite countermodel on the fixed product alphabet rather than an inconclusive failure code.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(N_m\), \(m\in\{0,1\}\), for the two finite role SCMs and \(Q\) for their common observational law on \(\prod_{i\in V}\mathcal A_i\).  For every \(k\in\mathbb Z\), take an independent copy \(N_m^k\), including an independent copy of every private or pairwise-shared exogenous root of \(N_m\).  If \(W_{m,s_i}^k\) denotes role \(s_i\) in copy \(k\), define
\[
 O_{m,i,t}:=W_{m,s_i}^{t-\tau_i},\qquad i\in V,\quad t\in\mathbb Z.
\]
This is well typed because there is exactly one role for coordinate \(i\), so \(O_{m,i,t}\in\mathcal A_i\), rather than in a product enlargement of \(\mathcal A_i\).

Consider a finite-role directed edge \(s_j\to s_i\).  Its lag is \(\ell=\tau_i-\tau_j\in\{0,\ldots,L\}\) by hypothesis.  At process time \(t\), the structural equation for \(O_{m,i,t}\) uses \(O_{m,j,t-\ell}\), and the copy indices agree because
\[
 (t-\ell)-\tau_j=t-(\tau_i-\tau_j)-\tau_j=t-\tau_i.
\]
The identical calculation realizes a shared root between two roles at the stipulated offset.  Thus all directed and shared-root spans are at most \(L\), establishing the refinement-span condition.  Positive-lag arrows strictly increase time, while the lag-zero coordinate union is acyclic by premise; hence every instantaneous slice is acyclic.  The structural tables are independent of \(t\), so the equations are time homogeneous.  Every exogenous root belongs to one copy, roots from distinct copies are independent, and every root still has at most two observed children.  Thus the semi-Markovian condition is preserved.  Finally, translating every finite-role edge through all \(t\) gives, by premise, exact summary \(H\).  These observations establish all graphical and structural parts of membership in \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\).

For strict stationarity, shifting every process time by \(h\) replaces every copy index \(t-\tau_i\) by \(t-\tau_i+h\).  The copies are identically distributed and independent over \(\mathbb Z\), so this relabeling leaves every finite-dimensional distribution unchanged.

It remains to prove equality and positivity of the entire process laws, rather than of a selected window.  Let \(D\subseteq V\times\mathbb Z\) be finite and let \(a_D\) be an assignment.  For every copy index \(k\), put
\[
 D_k:=\{s_i:(i,t)\in D,\ t-\tau_i=k\}.
\]
Only finitely many \(D_k\) are nonempty.  Independence across copies gives, for \(m=0,1\),
\[
 P_{M_m}\{O_{m,D}=a_D\}
 =\prod_{k:D_k\ne\varnothing}Q\{W_{D_k}=a_{D_k}\}.
\]
The right-hand side is independent of \(m\), proving equality on all finite cylinders.  Cylinder sets form the defining coordinate events of the common product space \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\), so the two process measures are equal.  Each factor is a marginal cell of the strictly positive joint law \(Q\), hence is positive; consequently every finite cylinder has positive probability.

Because \(\tau_X=-\gamma\), the intervened process variable \(O_{m,X,-\gamma}\) is precisely role \(s_X\) in copy \(0\).  Because \(\tau_Y=0\), \(O_{m,Y,0}\) is role \(s_Y\) in that same copy.  The intervention changes no equation in another copy.  Therefore
\[
 P_{M_m}(Y_0=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x))
 =P_{N_m}(s_Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(s_X=x)).
\]
The two quantities on the right differ by premise.  This proves the claimed separation and completes membership in \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\).
